title: Mycerinus
summary: Egyptian king, son of Cheops in Herodotus, who reopened the temples (2.129–134); Menkaure.
description: Added from the Herodotus import (The Histories, tr. Rawlinson). Herodotus gives reign lengths and synchronisms, not BC years, and no tier 1–4 chronology dates this person, so there is no sort year.

sorting_basis.note: No tier gives a birth year (Herodotus is display-only and gives none).

birth.note: pending CFAH reference (no CFAH anchor point or Table 1 entry found for this)

death.citation: Griffith & White, "Chronological Framework of Ancient History. 6: The Old and Middle Kingdoms of Egypt," ARJ 18 (2025): 13–60, section "B. The Great War links Dynasties 2, 4, 5, 9, 10, and 11: 1825–1769 BC"
death.note: Menkaure (Herodotus's Mycerinus) "lived 35 years into the Great War, thus dying about 1790 BC".

reign.date: Start Co-Rex: 1851; Start Sole-rex: 1825; End Sole-rex: ?; Death or Deposition: 1789

reign.date: “After Chephren, Mycerinus (they said), son of Cheops, ascended the throne.”
reign.citation: Herodotus, Histories 2.129 (tr. George Rawlinson; Roman Roads Media etext, 2013), p. 151 (PDF p. 153)

reign.date: “Egypt was fated to suffer affliction one hundred and fifty years”
reign.citation: Herodotus, Histories 2.133 (tr. George Rawlinson; Roman Roads Media etext, 2013), p. 153 (PDF p. 155)
reign.note: Oracle to Mycerinus (who was told he had six years to live). Internal: the oracle's 150 years against the 106 years of 2.128.

reign.citation: Raleigh, The History of the World (1617, EEBO-TCP A10357), Chronological Table, sig. 788a
reign.note: Year cell "3874 3192 199". The third printed figure 199 is the column "Temple", not a length. To the Reader (sig. 780b): the Julian Period exceeds the yeere of the World by 682. The 6 at the end of the name is the reign length he prints. The end year is not printed on this row. Column: Egypt..
